text:
Beckett Sennecke is 20, in his second NHL season, and already playing 20:31 a night for Anaheim, three minutes more than as a rookie. He has 21 points in 17 games, ten goals, and is on the ice for 81 percent of the Ducks' power-play chances (47 percent last year). He scored twice in Edmonton on November 5, and his teammates gave him a new nickname, "Macarooner", per a Dose.ca headline.

Put the breakout and the luck side by side. Of the 56 forwards picked in the top five since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median scored 0.54 points a game in their first full year. Sennecke is at 1.24. He will not stay there: he is shooting 23 percent (12 last season), and the Ducks have scored 12.8 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice.

The underlying talent looks legitimate. Evolving-Hockey rated his offensive impact in the 97th percentile among forwards last season, and he gets to the net (94th percentile in home-plate chances, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones). Our projection lands around 81 points. The defensive side is the thing to watch.
headline: Sennecke has arrived early
